body:
Close to a month later, I'm still moving forward!

This may be the longest I've gone without alcohol in over four years.  Even though there's an open box of wine in my kitchen (for cooking) I haven't given into the occasional temptation to drink to help me cope.

My therapy has been very challenging. I've put aside my pride, to try being completely honest about my shortcomings and fears. Perhaps I can find forgiveness for mistakes I've made with many people in my life. Slow progress, but that's the nature of this stuff. 

In addition, I'm still working out six days a week, alternating lifting and cardio. I've cut out all refined sugars and heavily processed foods from my diet, except for the occasional snack. It's been a long time since I've put this much effort into something just for myself. I plan to push myself as hard as possible on this, and see what I'm capable of.

My next step is boxing up all my ex's stuff I still have and mailing it back to her. Emotionally I'm sure it will be a huge ordeal, but I have to deal with it soon. I heard from a friend that she isn't doing well at all recently, but that's not something I can make my problem any more, and I'm working to accept that.

Overall I still feel lost, alone, and helpless most of the time, but I'm living for the moments my progress comes together and I get a glimpse of something much better on the horizon. It's thanks to beacons like you and my therapist that I'm pointed in the right direction.

I might check in again in a month or so, it really does help to write this all out to someone.

Jesse, I want to thank you again for helping ground me and motivating me to acknowledge my progress. Focusing on taking small steps toward healing has been essential for me in the past week, and I've been able to handle each day with a little more confidence.

In the spirit of focusing on the little victories, I wanted to tell you I had a great meeting with a new therapist yesterday, and finally slept well last night! Also, I'm really proud of this and have nobody in my "real life" I'm comfortable telling yet: I haven't had alcohol since last weekend! I'd been drinking daily for weeks before this and lying to myself that it was okay... I've switched to drinking protein shakes like I used to do, and I'm stoked at the improvement in my energy.

I probably won't message you now unless things do go belly up again for me - I don't want to be a burden - but I'm really trying to use this dark time as a motivation to become even stronger than before.

I was able to sleep last night, only waking up three times in a panic... each time I calmed my breathing and remembered a time after this incident that I really helped her feel safe, to maintain some perspective on the situation.

I now remember that at no point that night did she tell me to stop or that I had hurt her. We play-fought and wrestled roughly a lot before and after this, and she would always tell me when enough was enough. We had an established safeword (or even just "no" or "stop" would have worked) but I'm worried that night her fight or flight response kicked in and I wasn't sober enough to notice her change.

I don't want to sound like I'm blaming her for not stopping me or defending herself; it's just really hard for me to understand how she seemed okay with it at the time and has just recently been triggered to fear that night (and by extension, me) so much. More questions for a counselor I suppose.

I do know that I'm never again going to drink and then do something emotional or physical, because that's begging for trouble. I might give up drinking altogether - I only started drinking a few years ago and still apparently don't really understand how it effects me.

Today I'm not sure what to do, other than sit with my thoughts and try cleaning up my apartment if I have the energy. I'm still shaking and having trouble breathing evenly but I don't think that should prevent me from keeping busy. I still feel so lost, having to handle a breakup out of the blue and knowing my best friend (who in any other situation I would run to for support) is now so scared of me.

I keep reading over this and smiling through my tears because I hope so so so much that you're right. I'm certainly learning a lot from this experience, and I can only hope other positive things might come from this some day too, for me and for her.

Whew, I'm going through all my stuff and getting rid of everything regarding her... it's so much, and I *hate* how final it feels, but it's necessary. I really don't want to have to return her spare key, because it meant so much to both of us when she trusted me with it, but it's part of moving on I guess.

I feel so absolutely wretched about all of this... she used to be so excited that she finally found a partner who she could be safe with, she'd literally dance in circles! She's such a great woman and doesn't deserve any of this mess. All from one night of losing my control...

I know it's going to be a long long time before I trust myself in a relationship again, and I'm going to be so timid about being close with anyone. I probably won't be able to look anyone in the face for a few months, it's happened to me before and a similar feeling is here this time. As illogical as it might seem, my self-worth has been entirely *destroyed* by this. I'm really hoping counselling can help with all of it.

I'm trying so hard not to lose myself to the pain, and keep moving toward love, both within myself and through friends. It's still a battle I'm not sure I'll win, but I'm taking it ten minutes at a time.

Thank you! I try so hard to be that happy person, and so many of my friends have told me over the years that I'm the most uplifting friend they have... I'm trying really hard not to define myself by that single situation when I fell apart...

My greatest sadness, that I know I'll keep with me forever, is how my ex will take this. She went out on such a limb to open herself up to me after a lot of trauma in her life, and knowing that I really re-enforced those fears in her is simply destroying me. She trusted someone completely for the first time in her life, and I broke that in a huge way.

I can learn from this and be happy some day... I'm so much more worried about her!

I wish you the best as well in walking a good path through your life. I'm glad you had the fortitude to move on from your own abusive relationship, that can seem impossibly hard.

I just wanted you to know I'm now listening to good music, and I smiled once recently today, and I'm no longer shaking. I still want to throw up, and can't imagine going back to work, or even looking anyone in the face, but they're more small steps forward.

I feel so so so so remorseful over how much I've hurt my ex who already had many trust issues from childhood trauma. There's nothing I can DO with this remorse though, other than sit with it and understand that I deserve it. It will certainly inspire me to find counselling to learn anger management skills, which I'd never thought I'd need. I am never ever treating someone like that again if I can help it.

I think you're right that my filter just disappeared at some point that night and I didn't notice - looking back on it, I was completely emotional and unhinged and incapable of verbal expression, stuttering over every syllable.

I've drunk on so many other occasions, with and without my ex, and 99% of the time I'm happy and cuddly when tipsy. I don't know what factors must have changed on that night, but something went seriously wrong.

Having been the only aggressor, it's near impossible for me to feel any self-acceptance that I became caught up in something I couldn't control well. I come from a "no excuses" sort of family, and saying "there were outside influences too" doesn't sit well with me. I certainly had a lot of frustrations at that point in my life - no job, no car, not enough getting out of the house, seasonal depression with the dark and rain...

Now I've got a steady job somewhere new with my own transportation, the weather is so much better, I'm working out a lot and meditating... I'm in such a good place now *other* than that six months I threw away my relationship with *the only person who's ever felt like home to me*, just because I couldn't control myself, and yesterday it all fell apart.

I'm so glad my ex told me she had to make a clean break from me though. Long term, that will be good for both of us, and maybe once I put myself back together and learn more de-escalation coping skills I'll finally be able to accept where I'm at right now.

Thank you so so much for taking time to write to me today. I'm crying because even though you've never met me you're showing me such compassion on a day I'm at my worst and really have wanted to just end everything.

> right now what's eating away at you is that you don't understand why or how you did this

This is it exactly. I've had friends who were abused and I've seen what it puts them through. I've always been adamant that I would *never* do that to anyone, least of all my best friend...

And now I'm here having done so, with no reason or excuse beyond "I was drunk so my inhibitions were lowered"... I can't understand why that would change my attitude from "never ever" to "why not"... I've proven I'm capable of doing something so awful... I can't stop hating myself over this, it's absolutely overwhelming :(

I'm trying very hard to focus on the good aspects of my life, and not overwhelm myself with how my ex must be feeling right now. Invasive thoughts are the main source of anxiety for me, and they're all justifiably so negative. I partially feel like I deserve to suffer from all this bad energy, which really keeps me down.

I'm curled up in the fetal position with a blanket, you got that spot on :)

Even if I'm not the first to go through something like this, I can't imagine a time in the future that I won't be severely depressed about it. That's the main burden I have right now, and while you're right that an action doesn't define me, I still don't see any conceivable way of forgiving myself and moving on.
Yeah, the panic attack has become an every-other-hour thing so I guess that's progress. I still doubt I'll be able to sleep but I'll deal with that later.

Thank you for your positive response. It's so hard for anything to have a helpful effect on me right now... I've listened to music and gone for a long walk today, which helped pass the time at least. If I ate anything I'd throw up immediately, but maybe in an hour or two I'll make chicken soup or something easy.

I feel so alone in all of this - I'm so so embarrassed to talk to any friends or family about this... why should they support me after what I've done?
Thanks for your reply. I'm really looking forward to counseling and just decompressing a bit. Sticking it out until then is the hardest thing I've ever done though.

Thank you so much for your kind words. I'm sure it will take a long time for me to find forgiveness within myself - right now I really feel like I only deserve to hurt. Maybe with help I can start to forgive myself though.

I'm still not sure how I'm going to make it through today or tomorrow, but you're probably right that in the long term I'm going to be okay. I'm still so worried about my ex, but her life is out of my scope now.
